authority_statement: Informational report only; the deterministic LFighter pipeline retains all security decision authority.
executive_summary: In this development-and-validation case, the plain DDoS-to-Benign prediction rate exceeded the paired clean rate; the defended rate was lower than the plain rate. Reconstruction attribution distance decreased toward a paired preattack clean reference, not an oracle clean state.

facts.statement: The plain attack mean DDoS-to-Benign prediction rate was 0.343306, versus 0.077628 in the paired clean branch.
The defended mean DDoS-to-Benign prediction rate was 0.080254, an absolute reduction of 0.263053 from the plain attack branch.
Mean and minimum malicious recall were 1.000000, and maximum benign false-positive rate was 0.000000.
Normalized attribution distance decreased from 0.837453 to 0.306140, with recovery fraction 0.634439.

interpretations.statement: The observed prediction behavior is consistent with targeted suppression of DDoS predictions toward the Benign class, but does not establish malicious intent.
Reconstruction moved the attribution profile toward its paired preattack clean reference; this is not evidence of oracle clean restoration.

refusals: Refused: the evidence does not support a claim of verified malicious intent.
Refused: the evidence does not support a claim of exact oracle clean recovery.
uncertainties: The clean attribution comparator is a paired round 4 preattack reference, not an oracle clean state.
Rejected and oracle-clean attribution states were unavailable and were not substituted.
Per-client detector scores and numeric detector thresholds were not materialized.
The evidence is limited to development and validation; reserved test arrays remained closed.
